alt: Jobs shown by processing time. An adjacent out-of-order pair is marked, then swapped shortest first, with the drop in their combined finish time labeled, then the whole list settles into shortest-first order.

steps.caption: These jobs run one after another on a single machine, in the order they arrive.
Jobs at positions 0 and 1 are out of order: 7 runs before 3. Only their own two finish times change if they swap, and those add up to 2 x 7 + 3 = 17.
Swap them, shortest first: their two finish times now add up to 2 x 3 + 7 = 13, which is 4 less. Putting the shorter job first never costs more, and strictly helps whenever the jobs differ.
Repeating this swap at every out-of-order adjacent pair, each time strictly improving or leaving the total unchanged, ends with the whole list shortest first.
Sorted shortest first: 2, 3, 7, 9. The sum of every finish time is 40, the smallest possible for these jobs.
